- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or overshoots mid-cycle; apply smoothing filter to avoid sharp peaks.
- After a price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next 3–5 days; dampen forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; lag forecast by 1–2 days to align with sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when price deviates >10% from 18-day moving average; cap forecast within ±10% of moving average unless sentiment overrides.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) and price is rising, model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underpredicts; increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
